title: Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence (Executive Order)
key_claim: Executive order directs the Attorney General to set up an AI Litigation Task Force within 30 days to challenge state AI laws, instructs Commerce to condition BEAD broadband funding on states' AI rules, and directs a legislative recommendation for a uniform federal framework preempting conflicting state AI laws (carve-outs for child safety, data-centre infrastructure, state procurement).
signals_supported: US federal pre-emption of state AI law

title: New Skills and AI Are Reshaping the Future of Work
date_evidence: Author byline 'Kristalina Georgieva' followed by dateline 'January 14, 2026'
key_claim: One in 10 job postings in advanced economies and one in 20 in emerging markets now require at least one new skill; nearly 40 percent of global jobs are exposed to AI; employment in AI-vulnerable occupations is 3.6 percent lower after five years in high-AI-skill-demand regions; Finland, Ireland and Denmark rank highest on the IMF Skill Readiness Index.

title: Artificial intelligence: Council and Parliament agree to simplify and streamline rules
date_evidence: Search result and corroborating legal analyses: 'On 7 May 2026, the European Parliament and the Council of the EU reached a provisional agreement on the Digital Omnibus on AI', postponing standalone high-risk (Annex III) obligations from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027.
key_claim: Council and Parliament reached a provisional Digital Omnibus agreement on 7 May 2026 postponing standalone high-risk AI obligations from August 2026 to December 2027, deferring embedded high-risk product obligations to August 2028, extending SME simplifications to small mid-caps (up to 500 employees), and adding new prohibitions on AI-generated non-consensual intimate material and CSAM.
signals_supported: EU AI Act simplification and deadline delay

title: The OECD AI exposure measure
date_evidence: OECD AI exposure measure publication page; the measure maps AI capabilities across nine domains to occupational requirements and finds occupations at highest risk of automation account for about 28 percent of jobs across OECD countries, with low-skilled, young and male workers most exposed.
key_claim: The OECD AI exposure measure, built on the OECD AI Capability Indicators, finds AI capabilities are closest to routine information-processing and administrative work; occupations at highest risk of automation account for about 28 percent of jobs across OECD countries, and most exposed workers will not need specialised AI skills but will see their tasks change.

title: Inside the AI Index: 12 Takeaways from the 2026 Report
date_evidence: Author 'Shana Lynch' with dateline 'April 13, 2026' on the article page

title: State of AI trust in 2026: Shifting to the agentic era
date_evidence: Insights page carries no visible publication date; content anchors it to the '2026 AI Trust Maturity Survey. Taken between December 2025 and January 2026' of approximately 500 organizations.
key_claim: McKinsey's 2026 AI Trust Maturity Survey (c.500 organizations, Dec 2025 to Jan 2026) finds average responsible-AI maturity rose to 2.3 from 2.0; nearly two-thirds cite security and risk concerns as the top barrier to scaling agentic AI; AI incident frequency held steady at roughly 8 percent but confidence in incident response declined; knowledge and training gaps are the leading barrier to implementation.
signals_supported: Agentic AI from pilots to production

date_evidence: Byline 'Ram Iyer' with timestamp '6:30 AM PDT · April 24, 2026'
key_claim: DeepSeek released preview versions of DeepSeek V4 (Pro at 1.6 trillion parameters, the biggest open-weight model available) which it says has almost closed the gap with leading models on reasoning, trailing frontier models by roughly 3 to 6 months on knowledge tests; V4 Flash is priced at $0.14 per million input tokens, undercutting frontier peers, underscoring China's sovereign-AI and inference-cost trajectory.

title: EU AI Act Deadlines 2026-2027: Compliance Calendar + Fines
key_claim: The EU AI Act phases obligations across multiple dates: prohibited practices since February 2025, GPAI model obligations since 2 August 2025, and high-risk system obligations originally set for 2 August 2026, with maximum fines of EUR 35 million or 7 percent of global turnover for prohibited practices.
signals_supported: EU AI Act simplification and deadline delay

title: The automation illusion: Why AI is making COOs' jobs harder, not easier
date_evidence: meta og:url /2026/06/01/ and visible dateline 'June 1, 2026, 7:37 PM ET' (author Nick Lichtenberg)

title: Electricity 2026: Analysis and forecast to 2030
date_evidence: IEA Electricity 2026 report landing page; the report finds global data-centre electricity demand grew 17 percent in 2025 and AI-focused data-centre consumption surged about 50 percent, with data-centre electricity use set to roughly double by 2030 and AI-focused use to triple.
key_claim: IEA Electricity 2026 finds data-centre electricity demand grew 17 percent in 2025, AI-focused data-centre consumption surged about 50 percent, and data-centre electricity use is set to roughly double to around 945 TWh by 2030, with nearly 20 percent of planned data-centre projects globally facing grid-connection delays.
